metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets – Estonia

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Estonia using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of students within schools across participating countries and economies, and OECD reporting typically relies on the PISA sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates and correct standard errors. The factsheet itself does not specify the exact weight variable name (e.g., student design weight) or whether replicate weights were used, so the precise weighting implementation cannot be confirmed from the provided text. The reported uncertainty is presented as 95% confidence intervals, and some comparisons are flagged with asterisks when PISA sampling standards were not met, indicating that technical quality criteria affect interpretability.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable here because the provided text is a country factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking performance and descriptive/benchmark comparisons, rather than documenting an analysis pipeline that uses PV-based achievement estimates. The factsheet also does not report any missing-data strategy (e.g., imputation or deletion rules) because it is not presenting a methodological ML estimation procedure. As a result, the missing-data handling details are not available in the excerpted content.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the Estonia analytic sample of 15-year-old students who completed the PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment (completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 13 300 15-year-olds; Estonia: 6,392 students in 196 schools). The factsheet does not describe additional exclusions beyond PISA’s standard implementation and technical standards; it notes that some countries/economies with an asterisk (*) require caution due to not meeting sampling standards.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes Estonia’s performance on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking cognitive test for 15-year-old students. The creative thinking assessment contains 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas—across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. Estonia’s mean creative thinking score is 36/60, which is significantly higher than the OECD average (33). The factsheet reports proficiency distribution (89% at least Level 3; 34% at Level 5–6) and relative strengths by ideation process and domain context, including higher relative performance in tasks requiring generating creative ideas and in written/visual/scientific problem-solving contexts. It also documents within-Estonia gaps by socio-economic status and gender, and reports associations with mathematics and reading performance, while flagging interpretive caution for countries/economies that did not meet PISA sampling standards.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a descriptive OECD factsheet rather than an empirical ML study: it does not specify an ML model, training procedure, or predictive target variable, and it does not provide a methodological section for PV handling or missing-data treatment. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques and structured predictive findings are intentionally left empty, while the outcome summary focuses on PISA benchmark results, proficiency levels, and correlational/relative comparisons reported by OECD.
